title.value: Wrap a 90s inventory system with a modern workflow

introduction.value: A business owner used Claude to check prices against invoices, book items into stock, send customer reminder emails and plan purchase orders on legacy inventory software.

method.value: The owner connected Claude to a 1990s inventory system through a Synology-hosted connector using MCP and a VPN to reach the central database, after getting server keys from IT. Built in about three weeks using prompts, it lets Claude compare invoice prices, book stock, change item prices, build dashboard-style interfaces from system data, and suggest purchase orders from daily sales, five years of history, and trends; the owner reviews the proposed change list and reasoning, then approves once before writes happen.

outcome.value: They say it saves 2–3 hours a day and has become the main interface while the legacy software stays in the background. It is not fully hands-off: the owner still handles customer emails personally or only uses AI drafts because the model can include information that should stay internal.

notes.value: The main catch is access and oversight: they needed server credentials from IT, spent three weeks getting it working, and still read the before-and-after changes plus Claude’s reasoning before approving writes.

source_text.body:
Wrap a 90s inventory system with a modern workflow
A business owner used Claude to check prices against invoices, book items into stock, send customer reminder emails and plan purchase orders on legacy inventory software.
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The owner connected Claude to a 1990s inventory system through a Synology-hosted connector using MCP and a VPN to reach the central database, after getting server keys from IT. Built in about three weeks using prompts, it lets Claude compare invoice prices, book stock, change item prices, build dashboard-style interfaces from system data, and suggest purchase orders from daily sales, five years of history, and trends; the owner reviews the proposed change list and reasoning, then approves once before writes happen.
How it went
They say it saves 2–3 hours a day and has become the main interface while the legacy software stays in the background. It is not fully hands-off: the owner still handles customer emails personally or only uses AI drafts because the model can include information that should stay internal.
Worth knowing
The main catch is access and oversight: they needed server credentials from IT, spent three weeks getting it working, and still read the before-and-after changes plus Claude’s reasoning before approving writes.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I run a small business using older inventory software that has [export format, e.g. CSV exports or a database file]. Using the files in [folder path], write a script or workflow that compares supplier invoice prices against my stock records, lists mismatches, and drafts a purchase order suggestion for items below [reorder level]. Don't change any stock records or send any emails automatically: show me the proposed changes and draft customer reminder emails for approval first. A finished job is a report I can review plus a script I can rerun each week.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1xte43d/how_i_used_claude_to_take_over_a_90sera_inventory
